thread.title: Calibration Review Part 5
thread.preview:
**We are not reopening the Wizard’s casting rules. We are correcting a Wizard’s recorded state in one spell-testing example.** The distinction got buried under the review terminology.

The example tests **Dimensional Break** against a target protected by **Dimensional Anchor**. A supporting level-7 Wizard cast the Anchor beforehand. That lets the encounter test whether Anchor blocks exile while leaving the force damage intact.

The inconsistency is in that supporting Wizard’s sheet:

| What the example records | What the sheet incorrectly records |
|---|---|
| The Wizard already cast Dimensional Anchor and paid **7 RP**, going from **24 to 17**. | Its list of prepared spell families already used is **empty**. |
| That casting used the family’s first-cast Dissonance exemption. | The empty list could incorrectly make that exemption available again. |

**I recorded the cast but omitted the corresponding spent-family entry. Codex caught that mismatch.** It is an error in my worked example, not a newly discovered design problem with your Wizard class. The :chatgpt-content-reference{index="0"}[latest correction request](sandbox:/mnt/data/DD_Rank8_Damage6_Cast_History_Correction_02.zip) expressly limits the work to that qualification and preserves the eight earlier corrections.

The necessary repair is to record **Dimensional Anchor’s family as already used in this encounter**, update the nine copies of that supporting actor, and check one lawful later casting to confirm it cannot receive the first-family exemption twice. **The original damage, RP and exile outcomes can remain unchanged.**

That exemption concerns **Dissonance, not a free spell or an RP refund**.

**This should be one bookkeeping correction and a follow-up check—not another Wizard casting review, class redesign or round of owner decisions.**

The Wizard’s protected interface grants **zero base Dissonance on the first casting of each prepared matrix family within an encounter**. | Field | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `matrixFamiliesUsed` | `[]` | `["dimensional-anchor"]` |
| `initialSetup` | Original disclosed −1 casting | The **entire original statement retained**, followed by an explicit same-encounter qualification |

The original casting remains correctly recorded as **24→17 RP, zero base Dissonance, Refrain 0**, with previous spell **Dimensional Anchor** and original concentration deadline **59**. **No Action flag is changed by this repair.**

The affected copies are the main RD8-05-B and its eight branches: CHA, FORCEDEFENSE, DEATH, NULLZERO, ONECELL, LIFELINK, COUNTER and HISTORY.

Their independent-reset and explicit-override semantics remain intact. A branch that removes the field’s current existence does not thereby erase the disclosed paid casting history or create an encounter reset.

The complete corrected case agrees across **MODEL, CASE_DISPOSITIONS and the Director’s full case block**. The player chapter remains byte-identical because this correction changes a supporting-actor fixture, not a player rule.

## 2. Separate later same-family diagnostic

The new diagnostic is **independent of the existing main and branch timelines**. The inventory remains **12 main cases and 42 branches**.

It uses the same actual **Wizard7**, the already acquired and prepared **rank-four Dimensional Anchor**, its **7 RP** cost and actual **V/S/F** components. A regular turn from **6 to 8** is explicitly supplied, with one available ordinary Action. This is a fixture scheduling premise—not an extra Action or an inference that elapsed seconds automatically create turns.

The caster’s origin `[40,0,3]` is squared distance **109** from the perceived point `[30,0,0]`, within the spell’s 60-foot range. Line of effect is clear. No suppression or interruption is supplied in the positive case.

| Time | Actual transition |
|---:|---|
| **6** | The supplied regular START completes. The Action is available; the used-family and previous-spell records remain. |
| **6.05** | Commit Dimensional Anchor once: **17→10 RP**, Action spent, **1 base Dissonance + 1 Refrain = 2 Dissonance**. |
| **6.05** | The new concentration commitment ends the old Anchor immediately. Its historical deadline remains 59; it is not refunded or reset. |
| **6.1** | The surviving new cast establishes a new field with its own deadline **66.1**. |
| **8** | No idle-turn Dissonance reduction applies, because this turn actually cast a spell. Final state remains **10 RP / Dissonance 2 / Refrain 1**. |

The real Reaction and Bonus Action remain unspent. HP, body, gear and position do not change. Dimensional Anchor requires no attack, save or damage roll here.

**The original empty-ledger error would yield Dissonance 1—not 0:** it wrongly waives the repeated family’s base point, but the already-recorded previous spell still produces Refrain 1. The corrected diagnostic proves that distinction.

Atomic controls also cover unavailable Action, unavailable prepared source, insufficient RP and invalid components/perception/geometry. A finite counter-after-commit control preserves the paid costs, casting history and old-concentration loss; it does not claim an implemented Counterspell encounter.
